official.deadline_note: The 26 January 2027 date is the scholarship deadline for 2027 entry applicants who apply by it; the earlier admission (UCAS) deadline for 2027 entry is 6pm UK time on 15 October 2026, and an offer of a place is a precondition for scholarship consideration. Deferred-entry applicants must apply in January of the year they will actually start; the University can only consider an undergraduate scholarship application once.
official.status_note: Applications for 2026 entry are now closed. Details on how to apply for 2027 entry will be made available on the official page in January 2027; selection takes place in April 2027 and outcomes are communicated by the end of May 2027.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published value: 'Course fees, a grant for living costs and one return air fare per year', supported for 3 or 4 years depending on course length. No monetary figure is published.
benefits: One return air fare per year
3 or 4 years of support depending on course length
eligibility: Be a national of a country that receives official development assistance from the Development Assistance Committee (DAC) of the OECD - the eligible country list is published on the official page
Be from a low-income country and be unable, for political or financial reasons or because suitable educational facilities do not exist, to study for a degree in your own country
Be a new undergraduate student; all subjects in the course listing are eligible except medicine
Have received an offer of a place at Oxford - the University cannot consider scholarship applications from students without an offer
Be of the highest academic ability; financial need, social commitment and lack of ability to study for a degree in your own country are also major criteria for selection
Intend to return to your country following your studies; priority is given to students who have not studied at undergraduate level before
requirements: Apply for admission to the University (UCAS, 15 October 2026 deadline for 2027 entry) and secure an offer before the scholarship can be considered
Apply for the scholarship by the 26 January 2027 deadline for 2027 entry, using the details published on the official page in January 2027
Write an annual report about your academic and social activities and achievements at the University
Maintain satisfactory academic progress - receipt of the award in subsequent years is subject to it
Apply only once - deferred-entry holders apply in January of the year they start, and the University can only consider applications for undergraduate scholarships once
documents: Oxford undergraduate application (UCAS) and a subsequent offer of a place
The separate Reach Oxford scholarship application, which is published on the official page in January 2027
Evidence of financial need and of inability to study for a degree in your own country
Evidence of social commitment and of the highest academic ability
English language proficiency evidence (unless exempt), to be shown by 31 July in the year of the offer

Lack of ability to study for a degree in your own country
Applicants should intend to return to their country following their studies

application_method: Apply for admission to the University via UCAS and secure an offer of a place
Complete the separate Reach Oxford scholarship application published on the official page in January 2027
official.application_route: Apply to Oxford through UCAS first (2027 entry deadline 15 October 2026, 6pm UK time) and hold an offer, then submit the separate Reach Oxford application published on the official page in January 2027.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be nationals of countries that receive official development assistance from the OECD Development Assistance Committee (DAC); the full country list is published on the official page.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scheme is designed for nationals of low-income DAC-listed countries studying at Oxford; eligibility is nationality-based rather than residency-based.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: All subjects in the Oxford undergraduate course listing are eligible except medicine.
official.duration: 3 or 4 years depending on course length
official.description: A number of Reach Oxford scholarships (formerly Oxford Student Scholarships) are offered to students from low-income countries who, for political or financial reasons, or because suitable educational facilities do not exist, cannot study for a degree in their own countries. Applicants must apply for admission to the University first: the University is unable to consider any scholarship applications from students who have not been offered a place at Oxford.
official.program_type: Undergraduate scholarship for candidates from low-income countries who cannot study for a degree in their own country
official.english_requirement: IELTS Academic 7.5 overall (minimum 7.0 per component) or TOEFL iBT 110 (Listening 22, Reading 24, Speaking 25, Writing 24); TOEFL tests taken from 21 January 2026 are not accepted and are currently under review. Also accepted: Oxford Test of English (Advanced) 165, C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 191 (min 185 per component), Pearson PTE Academic 76 (min 66 per skill), Trinity ISE III with distinction or ISE IV with pass in each section, and English Language GCSE/IGCSE at the published grades. Evidence is not needed at UCAS application but must be shown by 31 July in the year of the offer. Exemptions apply to citizens and residents of majority English-speaking countries recognised by UKVI, to the IB taught in English, to the Singapore Integrated Programme, and to applicants educated full-time in English for at least the two most recent years. Superscoring across test sessions is not accepted.

verification.notes: Read the official Reach Oxford page and Oxford's undergraduate English language and visa requirements page directly on ox.ac.uk; Oxford publishes the award's covered components (course fees, living costs grant, one return air fare per year) but no monetary figure.

applicant_utility.summary: Reach Oxford covers course fees, a living costs grant and one return air fare per year for 3-4 years, but Oxford publishes no monetary figure, so treat it as fee coverage plus an unspecified living stipend when comparing offers. Only around 2-3 awards are made each year and you must already hold an Oxford offer before the scholarship can be considered, so the first deadline that matters is the UCAS admission deadline of 15 October 2026, not the scholarship form. Watch the official page in January 2027 for the application details and submit by 26 January 2027; selection runs in April 2027 with outcomes by the end of May 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A first-time undergraduate applicant from a DAC-listed low-income country who cannot study for their degree at home, is applying to Oxford for 2027 entry in any subject except medicine, and can evidence both top academic ability and genuine financial need.
application_readiness_checklist: Submit your UCAS application by 6pm UK time on 15 October 2026 for 2027 entry - an offer is a precondition for any scholarship consideration
Book an accepted English test early (IELTS Academic, C1 Advanced, PTE and similar) and sit all components in one session, since superscoring is not accepted
Draft your evidence of financial need and of why you cannot study for a degree in your own country before the January 2027 application window opens
Document social commitment with dates, roles and referees you can cite in the scholarship form
Check whether your chosen college participates; not all colleges offer the scheme every year, but a transfer can be arranged if yours does not
Plan around the single-application rule: you can only be considered for an Oxford undergraduate scholarship once
common_rejection_risks: Applying for medicine or to a subject outside the eligible course listing
Failing to evidence financial need or inability to study at home - both are major selection criteria, not formalities
Missing the 26 January 2027 scholarship deadline because application details only appear on the page in January 2027
Assuming a deferred-entry holder can apply in the original cycle - deferred applicants apply in January of the year they actually start
Letting English evidence slip past the 31 July deadline in the year of the offer, or relying on component scores from different test sessions
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The scheme states course fees, a living costs grant and one return air fare per year, but publishes no monetary figure, so the real size of the living grant is unknown until an award is made. Visa fees, the Immigration Health Surcharge and any personal costs beyond the living grant are not addressed by the scholarship page and would remain the student's responsibility.
document_audit: English test certificates must be single-session and valid; Oxford explicitly refuses superscored component scores
TOEFL sittings from 21 January 2026 onwards are not accepted, so check the test date before booking a TOEFL slot
Financial-need evidence must match your own circumstances; a vague hardship statement will not carry the 'unable to study in own country' criterion
If you claim an English exemption (IB taught in English, or educated in English for the two most recent years), the waiver form goes to your offer-holding college, not to a central scholarship office
Astrophoria Foundation Year applicants must apply in the January before their undergraduate course starts, not before the Foundation Year itself
alerts: The real first deadline is the UCAS admission deadline of 15 October 2026 - no offer, no scholarship consideration at all
Competition is very high at around 2-3 awards per year, and Oxford states it has no additional funding for candidates who are not offered a scholarship
You can only be considered for an Oxford undergraduate scholarship once, including if you defer entry or progress from the Astrophoria Foundation Year
Applications for 2026 entry are closed; every detail for the next cycle appears on the official page in January 2027
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply through UCAS by 15 October 2026 and hold an Oxford offer, then submit the separate Reach Oxford application (published on the official page in January 2027) by 26 January 2027; selection is in April 2027 and outcomes arrive by the end of May 2027.
